extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: A new benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages. It covers 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains, and 4 task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval.
extraction.license: Permissive license that allows the use and redistribution of the data for research purposes
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.publisher: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S groups several multilingual speech datasets (MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14). For the new Fleurs dataset, 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest publicly available sets were used, and between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence in 102 languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Missing recordings or replaced low-quality recordings are mentioned as slight improvements that may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Read audiobooks of Librivox (MLS), European Parliament sessions (VoxPopuli), FLoRes dev and devtest sets (Fleurs), e-banking domain spoken data (Minds-14), and CoVoST-2.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For Fleurs speech retrieval, the pool of transcription candidates is augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits were built with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences for train, dev, and test respectively. Scripts are provided to download and easily reproduce the preprocessing steps.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For Fleurs, between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence. Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Between one and three recordings for each sentence (2.3 on average) for the Fleurs dataset.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Updates will be made on the HuggingFace platform. A 2nd version of the dataset may include slight improvements and changes such as missing recordings or replaced low-quality recordings.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker identity (speaker ID) is present in the recordings.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: There is a performance discrepancy between European and African languages, which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in Western European languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels. Performance gaps exist across geographical groups.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Used for speech recognition, speech-to-text translation, speech classification, and speech retrieval. Practitioners should perform hyperparameter search and checkpoint selection on the dev set, and report performance on the test set.
